mechanisms.statement: RL-Math's weight change is small (0.24 % of weight norm) and, like any RL run's, concentrated in each matrix's top 8 singular directions (top-8 share 0.118-0.135 Math, 0.127 for LM-judge RL, 0.030 Think-SFT); those 8 input-output pairs carry the gain: base + 1.5x them matches RL per sample (hard328 0.642 vs 0.640, MATH-500 456 vs 457, fresh2026 48.25 vs 50.5 of 136) and under a 4-vote (216.3 vs 215.9 of 328), the extra 0.5x standing in for the other 88 % of the change, while equal-norm random, Think-SFT or pair-shifted rank-8 edits do nothing because the base's later layers amplify only RL's own pairs (3-6x random). The pairs hold three separable parts: a deliberative opening (late-MLP directions that read Okay/Wait/consider; the plain top-8 edit 427 vs random 197 of 500), a finishing part in direction 1 and layers 22-31 that cuts hard328 cap hits (20 % to 11-13 %, 5 % at 3x) but does not raise, and when enlarged lowers, the right rate of finished answers (0.63 at 1.5x, 0.51 at 3x, 0.41 at 4.5x), and an accuracy part in directions 2-8 and layers 0-10 that raises the finished right rate (0.63 to 0.73-0.79) while leaving cap hits at 19-25 %; only finishing plus accuracy together give RL's 0.64. The opening is what the three-token cue gives the untrained base: at RL step 100 the plain model scores like the cued base (417.5 vs 410.5 of 500), hits the cap as often and gains as much from a vote (+7.2 vs +7.6 points), and a plain-base answer that opens deliberatively is right as often as a cued one, so the cue alone buys 79 % of RL's MATH-500 gain (224 to 410.5, RL 460) while steps 100-2,800 add the finishing and accuracy parts (+42.5 of 500). The accuracy part lowers the per-step slip rate on every sample, including problems the base cannot solve: on hard328 problems where the cued base finished wrong the edit is right 36 % vs 23 % for a second base sample, and on problems the cued base gets 0 of 4 it captures 0.88 [0.69, 1.13] of RL's per-sample gain; on code, Code-RL's own pairs do this (+7 points pass among finished answers over random) and Math's do not (+1.5), though their extra passes fall on problems the base already passes in other samples. Inference changes reach this part only by selection and loop removal: T 1.0 removes the T 0.6 loops (52-63 % of long attempts), and because the cued base's wrong answers scatter (same-problem agreement 0.26) a vote over 4 adds about 7 points on MATH-500 (446-450 vs RL 460) and lifts hard328 from 161 to 195 of 328, but the base has no right sample on 26 of the 36 problems RL's vote wins and more tokens or loop-neuron zeroing finish answers without making them right, so about 9 points on hard328 (195 vs 224) stay out of inference reach. Hence new edit cells follow which part they carry, not their norm or module type: edits confined to direction 1 or layers 22-31 cut cap hits and lower finished accuracy as they grow, edits confined to directions 2-8 or layers 0-10 raise finished accuracy to about 0.75-0.80 on hard328 at the base's cap rate of about 0.2, any edit holding both at 1.25-1.5x lands within 3 points of RL per sample and per vote on every set, including problems the base never solves, and random, pair-shifted or Think-SFT rank-8 edits stay at the base.

The RL weight change is tiny and low-rank: 0.24 % of each matrix's norm (Think-SFT's is 25 %), about half the entries untouched, ~10-12 % of its squared norm in each matrix's top 8 singular directions (Think-SFT 2 %), a concentration that any on-policy RL makes (LM-judge General-RL 0.127 vs Math 0.135) rather than one an outcome reward forces. Those top-8 directions read an input subspace that every reasoning change shares (Think-SFT's change lies in it at 4.8x chance, Code-RL's 5x more than Think-SFT's, code text drives it 0.87 as much as math text) and write directions the next layer reads 1.4x above random whose effect is domain-specific (on code, Math's 1.5x directions add +1.5 points over a random rank-8 edit, Code's own +7), and per matrix they concentrate where Think-SFT's change does (rho 0.59), not where IF-RL's does (-0.01). Base + 1.5x those directions is RL, per sample and in votes, by raising right answers on problems the base already finishes rather than by a finish dial, bf16 artifact or partial per-sample switch: MATH-500 456 vs 457, hard328 200.25 vs 200.0 (vote 216 vs 216), fresh2026 48.25 vs 50.5, 0.88 of RL's per-sample edge where the cued base gets 0 of 4, +13.5 points on base-finished-wrong problems with only 26 % of the gain on cap hits, -1x drops finished-right from 70 % to 51.5 %, and the edit's wrong answers lean toward RL's (+0.29), while random and Think-SFT top-8 edits of equal size do nothing. The change has two parts: a switch into sustained deliberation that the base already owns and that RL completes in its first 100 steps (plain base 224/500, base + three-token cue 410.5, step 100 plain 417.5, same cap-hit rate and same +7-point vote gain as the cued base, and plain base answers that open deliberatively are as right as cued ones, -0.03), and a graded per-step slip reduction on long derivations that steps 100 to 2,800 add (+42.5/500; answers 1.6x the cued base's length, 2.9 points fewer cap hits, vote gain down to +2.8, deliberative and non-deliberative edited answers both above the base's). Inference alone reproduces the first part fully, because a prompt (or a one-tensor hand edit that writes the cue, 397 vs 410) only selects a mode the base has: the cue at T 1.0, where loops past 4,096 tokens drop from 0.52-0.63 at T 0.6 to 0.004, gives 79 % of RL's plain MATH-500 gain and 77 % off-domain, and votes help the base more than RL because its wrong answers are scattered slips (pair agreement 0.26; real-vs-merged vote +0.07 to +0.11), so about 18 of 29 points need no training. The second part, about 11 points (hard328 vote 195 vs 224; fresh2026 29.5 vs 50.5), cannot come from prompts, votes, sampling or longer caps because the base has no right sample on 26 of the 36 problems RL's vote wins, yet a rank-8 edit carries it; so edits along RL's top-8 directions should track RL at about 1.5x and stack on Think-SFT (+6.9 at 2x), a step-100 top-8 edit should add nothing over the cue, the cue should add almost nothing to the 1.5x-edited base, the edited base's vote gain should be RL-small (about +3, not the base's +7), and Math's directions should do no more for code than a random edit of equal norm.

RL-Math's weight change (0.24% of weight norm) does its work through its top-8 singular input-output pairs per matrix (about 12% of its squared norm): added at 1.5x to the cued base they reach RL on hard328 (64.2% against RL plain 64.0%, base 50.2%; vote +0.1 points) and capture 0.88 of RL's per-sample gain where the base gets 0 of 4, as a graded shift in every sample, while random rank-8, Think-SFT-top-8, base-own-top-8 or re-paired edits of the same norm give about nothing. The pairs do two separable jobs: late layers and direction 1 are a finish dial that cuts cap hits (20% to 11-14%) but leaves never-solved problems at a fresh base sample's 0.05 and lowers accuracy above 2x (late 3x and 4.5x: 48%, 32%), while directions 2-8 and layers 0-21 shift each next-step choice toward RL's, which cuts slips, lifts finished-wrong problems (23% to 33%) and never-solved ones (0 to 0.15 per sample), and makes the edit's wrong answers agree with RL's (+0.29 over the base). On-policy RL writes such pairs whatever the reward (top-8 share: LM-judge General-RL 0.127, Math 0.135, Think-SFT 0.030), in the matrices deliberative text drives (pattern follows Think-SFT, rho 0.59, not IF-RL) and on input directions the base already uses (Think-SFT's change 4.8x chance there, Code-RL's 5.2x Think-SFT's, code text drives them at 87% of math), with the reward choosing only the output side, so Code-RL's pairs lift plain math about halfway (157/250 against Math's 217) as a per-sample opening switch (deliberative m21 answers 94% right, others 36%) and Math's pairs barely help code (+1.5 points against Code's +7.0). Inference copies only the opening and the finishing, plus selection among the base's own samples: the three-token cue is the deliberative opening that the first 100 RL steps install (step-100 plain 417.5 against cued base 410.5 of 500, same cap-hit rate, same vote gain +7.2 against +7.6), T 1.0 removes the repetition loops of T 0.6 (loop share past 4,096 tokens 0.52-0.63 against 0.004), and a vote over 4 turns sometimes-right into right because wrong answers mostly scatter (pair agreement 0.22-0.26). So the base reaches the part of RL's gain on problems where it already writes a right sample (81% of the MATH-500 sample gap; vote 446-450 against RL 463-474) and misses the slip-rate part (hard328 vote 195 against RL 224, with no right base sample on 26 of the 36 problems RL's vote wins), and self-review, truncation, tie rules and text edits add 0-1.4 points because none changes the per-step choice distribution. Hence a new edit's effect is set by which true RL pairs it contains, not by its norm, module type or the base's accuracy: layers 0-21 or directions 2-8 put base-0-of-4 hard328 problems at 0.10-0.19 per sample (layers 0-10 alone with cap hits near the base's 20%), late-only or direction-1 edits cut cap hits to 11-14% but stay at 0.05 there, mismatched-pair, random, Think-SFT or base-own edits of equal norm stay within 3 points of the base, Code-RL pairs give about half of Math's lift on math, and every edit peaks near 1.5x and falls by 2x (MATH-500 456 to 448).

Edited-model accuracy at a stated edit norm follows the base plus the flat random-edit curve: on hard328 with the cue (T 1.0, one sample, seed 3000000) the base scores 164 and random rank-8 edits at sizes -1 to 3 (incl. two draws at 1.5x) score 152-167, mean about 160 with sd about 4, so any norm-matched 1.5x edit whose content I may not use gets about 160 with an interval of single-sample noise plus allowance for subspace structure (m smaller = more concentrated edit = slightly wider low tail); vote-over-k accuracy of the untrained cued base follows a log-k curve fitted to its own board points on the 328 (159.5 at 1, 188.5 at 4, 197 at 6, which fit vote(k)=159.5+20.9 ln k exactly) and checked on the stored explore-half rows (vote over 4 of samples 0-3 = 94 of 164, x2 = 188), with interval width from tie-breaking noise measured on those rows (plus or minus 5 on the half) and per-sample noise.

Accuracy of any edited base model comes from the untrained cued base's single-sample level on hard328 plus the spread of random weight edits at the stated norm (random rank-8 edits at sizes -1 to 3 score 158-167 of 328 with seed noise of about 5), so an edit whose content I may not use is forecast at the random-edit/base level with an interval covering that spread plus one-sample noise and some extra room for a norm concentrated in an m-dimensional subspace (m/d = 64/4096 or 8/4096); vote-over-k counts of the cued base come from its own vote curve on the 328 (159.5 at k=1, 188.5 at k=4, 197 at k=6, rising roughly linearly in ln k at about 21 problems per unit ln k, flattening the way MATH-500's curve did), extrapolated to k=8, and a vote-8 minus vote-4 gap is that extrapolation minus the k=4 point.

Base-model vote targets follow the cued base's own vote-over-k curve on the 328 (vote over 4 = 188.5 and over 6 = 197, result-c065a6), extended to k = 8 with the shape of the cued base's vote curve on MATH-500 computed from the stored 12-sample rows (explore half, mean over random k-subsets: 446.9 at 4, 456.6 at 6, 461.3 at 8, so the 6->8 step is 0.485 of the 4->6 step and the 8-4 gap is 1.485 times it), with intervals set by seed noise (one-sample seeds differ by up to 9 problems). An edit's accuracy at a given edit norm follows the cued base's one-sample score plus the slope in edit norm fitted on the random rank-8 edits of the same norm family on hard328 (sizes -1 to 3: 159, 158, 159, 167, 163 against base 164, i.e. flat, slope about 0); the subspace dimension m (chance overlap m/4096) is used only to widen the interval downward for the smaller m, since a fixed norm packed into fewer residual dimensions can damage outputs; nothing about the RL change enters.
